thread:
nina: Heads-up — planning a dark-launch variant for the new routing heuristics. want to agree on metric thresholds that should trigger an automatic rollback.
ajay: +1. can we scope this to 10% of traffic and only for non-critical tenants?
matt: prefer starting at 5% to limit blast radius and validate sample bias. also need tail-latency SLOs not just p95.
ivy: agreed on p99.5 and p99 tails. if those degrade > 30% relative to baseline for 5m we should cut traffic.
sam: how do we define baseline for a newly onboarded model where there is no long historical tail?
nina: use a rolling baseline from the stable variant for the same route, with a 15m warmup window. fallback if baseline is sparse.
ajay: what about error semantics? increase in 5xxs vs model-quality regressions (LLR drop) should be separate signals.
matt: yes — split signals into infra (latency, 5xx, gpu OOMs) and quality (score drop, hallucination rate). infra triggers immediate rollout cut; quality triggers staged rampdown + human review.
ivy: propose config surface: {"max_pct": "5","infra_threshold_pct": "30","infra_window_s": "300","quality_threshold_pct": "10","quality_window_s": "900","min_sample_count": "100"} — thoughts?
sam: min_sample_count is critical otherwise noisy p99 from small sample will flip. maybe 200 for p99.
nina: deploy-bot: run-decision-sim --variant=dark-v2 --baseline=stable --window=900 --min-samples=200
deploy-bot: simulation complete: projected false-positive rollback rate 2.8% at 5% traffic, 1.1% at 2% traffic.
ajay: simulation looks sane. we should also add a short-term hysteresis: require 2 consecutive windows before rollback to avoid flapping.
matt: agree. plus a progressive cool-off: if we rollback, lock the variant for 30m and cap subsequent dark launches to 2% for that route.
ivy: operational runbook snippet: "on auto-rollback, notify #oncall and create incident with priority P2; stash recent 1m trace snapshots and evaluation prompts."
sam: telemetry contract: variants must emit metrics: request_count, success_count, p50,p95,p99, token_cost, quality_score. quality_score is optional but required for any model that touches user-visible text.
nina: question — do we allow probabilistic sampling weighting (so weighting is not uniform across tenants)? canaries per-tenant could bias evaluation.
ajay: support per-tenant sample weights but require a stratified sampling flag to guarantee min_sample_count per tenant group.
matt: implementation note: decision surface lives in the router but requires an observability oracle to feed aggregated windows. prefer a small policy service that subscribes to metrics and emits roll/cut decisions via signed tokens.
ivy: security note: signed tokens plus immutable decision id to prevent accidental replay. also rate-limit decision changes per route.
sam: edge case: model-only regressions (quality drop) — should we fall back to synthetic post-processing (e.g., response reranking) instead of immediate rollback?
nina: yes — fallback graph should include mitigations: synthetic filters, cached-responses, degrade-longest-prompts. only after mitigations fail do we cut traffic.
matt: add observability contract for mitigation effectiveness so the policy can escalate.
ajay: final ask: document DSL for rollout policy in console. simple example:  
``` 
policy: {
  type: dark_launch,
  max_pct: 5,
  infra_trigger: {metric: p99_latency, pct: 30, window_s: 300, consecutive: 2},
  quality_trigger: {metric: quality_score, pct: -10, window_s: 900, consecutive: 2, min_samples: 200},
  mitigations: ["rerank","cache","shorter_prompt"],
  cooldown_s: 1800
}
```
ivy: I'll start a short RFC fragment with these knobs and a proposed console UI. tagging @sam @matt for review.
nina: thanks — please include simulation logs and the deploy-bot command outputs in the RFC.
deploy-bot: added simulation artifacts to the RFC thread: /rfc/architecture/dark-launch-v2/sim-1758024680
